data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["ML ensemble members are typically trained to convergence on the same objective; non-expert panel members have heterogeneous internal models shaped by training on the same checklist","The expert is not a 'strong classifier' in the same sense\u2014intuition may access features the checklist omits, unlike a model restricted to the same feature space","ML ensemble error independence is often engineered via bagging/boosting; panel error independence depends on cognitive diversity that shared checklist training may reduce"],"overturn_conditions":["Empirical demonstration that panel errors on incorrect items are conditionally independent even with shared checklist training","Proof that the checklist covers all discriminative features for the task domain","Evidence that expert intuition does not capture features omitted by the checklist"],"shared_structure":["Ensemble of weak classifiers (non-expert panel) vs. single strong classifier (expert)","Aggregation benefit depends on base member error independence","Checklist is analogous to a constrained feature set available to all base learners"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_005"],"transfer_claims":["The conditional independence of errors given the checklist determines whether aggregation produces genuine reliability gain","Shared feature omissions create correlated errors that bound ensemble reliability at the checklist's coverage ceiling","Error covariance on incorrect items reveals whether reliability gain comes from aggregation or mere coverage coincidence"]},"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following an explicit checklist will, on average, produce more reliable judgments for objectively verifiable outcomes if and only if the panel members' errors are conditionally independent given the checklist's specified features. The single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere compliance by measuring within-panel agreement on incorrect items: if errors cluster on specific non-checklisted cases (indicating shared systematic blind spots), the panel's reliability is bounded by checklist coverage rather than enhanced by aggregation; if errors are idiosyncratic and uncorrelated, aggregation drives reliability above any single member's baseline.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is incomplete relative to the task's discriminative features, and omitted features are systematically correlated with outcome determination.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Panel members' training is homogeneous, producing correlated errors rather than independent ones.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The single expert's intuition captures features omitted by the checklist, making the expert's errors orthogonal to the panel's shared blind spots.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The evaluation sample is dominated by cases the checklist handles well, masking the panel's systematic failures on uncovered cases.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist reduces variance by constraining the hypothesis space to articulable features, but it also introduces a shared bias: all panel members are trained on the same checklist, so their errors are correlated on any case whose discriminative feature lies outside the checklist's scope. A single expert's intuition may incorporate un-articulable pattern matching that captures these omitted features, making the expert's errors orthogonal to the panel's. For objectively verifiable outcomes, panel superiority holds only when aggregation can exploit independent errors. The single-evaluation discriminator is the covariance structure of panel errors: high within-panel agreement on incorrect answers reveals shared systematic blind spots (checklist compliance tracking the right answer only on cases the checklist happens to cover), while high within-panel disagreement on incorrect answers reveals idiosyncratic errors that aggregation can suppress.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
